rationale: While the paper addresses domestic water and sanitation in international development cooperation (c1 = yes), it is a critical/conceptual historical essay examining global quantitative target setting (1976 onward, the MDGs, and post-2015 measurement options) rather than an empirical primary study or systematic review (c3 = no, E05). It also neither examines a legal or administrative rule mechanism governing household/community service access under narrow Criterion 2 (c2_narrow = no) nor evaluates empirical water/sanitation access outcomes (c4 = no).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Under the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 reading, international development target setting and MDG indicator design clearly fail Criterion 2 (no domestic legal, regulatory, tenure, tariff, discretion, enforcement, or utility-structure mechanism). Under the literal/plain Criterion 2 wording, global MDG target setting could arguably touch broad international governance/institutional factors (unclear), but the decision remains exclude under both readings because the paper is a conceptual/critical essay on global measurement agendas without primary empirical evidence or systematic synthesis (E05) and does not evaluate empirical service-access outcomes.

evidence_quotes.quote: Quantifying Water and Sanitation in Development Cooperation: Power or Perversity?
In this paper, we critical analyze two early periods of target setting together with their most recent incarnation in the 2000/1 Millennium Development Goals (MDGs).
In a final section, we offer some brief conclusions on the implications for the post-2015 agenda and some potential alternative measurement routes to tread.
